ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-engagement screening of all beneficial owners, directors, authorised signatories and shareholders against the OFAC SDN List, the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, EU restrictive measures lists, the French national terrorism financing freeze list and domestic criminal record checks in accordance with Articles L.561-5 and L.561-10 of the French Monetary and Financial Code. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) must be identified using the FATF 40 Recommendations definition and treated with enhanced due diligence; any positive match or residual risk must be escalated to TRACFIN, the French financial intelligence unit, before the relationship is established.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr, with name availability verification performed against the Registre National du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) database via Infogreffe (infogreffe.fr).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name (dénomination sociale) must be capable of accurate transcription in Latin characters for registration in the RCS. A name in non-Latin script must be accompanied by an official Latin transliteration or a coherent French-language translation. The name must not be contrary to public order, must not mislead the public and should normally be in French, although a foreign expression may be accepted if the corporate object or the commercial character justifies it.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the competent registrar (greffier du tribunal de commerce) or the INPI rejects the proposed corporate name, the applicant may file a reasoned application for review before the juge commis à la surveillance du registre du commerce et des sociétés within one month of receiving the rejection, pursuant to Articles R.123-130 et seq. of the French Commercial Code. The applicant should annex the rejected name, a copy of the incorporation project, the search results from the RCS and INPI databases, and evidence of prior use or of the distinctive character of the chosen name. A fresh name may be filed immediately. If a name reservation has been granted and subsequently lapses, the reservation may be renewed one time subject to proof that the incorporation process is still actively ongoing; otherwise a new reservation application must be submitted.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible for administrative and statutory purposes under Article L.123-11-1 of the French Commercial Code, provided the domiciliation provider is approved by the Prefecture and maintains the registered address accessible during normal working hours. For the ISIC 4330 cleanroom modular interior fit-out contracting activity, a virtual office will be accepted during formation and for back-office operations; however, before entering into significant construction or cleanroom installation contracts, the actual execution premises, subcontracting capabilities and technical references must be demonstrated. Public contracts and certification bodies may require a physical operational address or a dedicated technical facility, so the incorporation plan should include a cost-effective shared technical office or documented operational base.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: The risk of unannounced physical on-site inspection is assessed at approximately 8% per annum for a low-risk contracting company without employees or with fewer than five administrative staff. The risk rises to 15-20% on active cleanroom fit-out worksites owing to Labour Inspectorate (Inspection du travail) and URSSAF site checks. If the company claims large VAT refunds, applies for construction industry credits or engages a high volume of sub-contractors, the probability of a joint audit and site visit increases to 25-30% within the first two fiscal years.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des finances publiques (DGFiP), principally through the relevant Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE) or the Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères (SIEE) for non-established businesses. Official tax portal: impots.gouv.fr; business formalities are filed through the Guichet unique operated by INPI at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SAS is registered through the Guichet unique. Registration results in assignment of a SIREN and establishment-specific SIRET; the SIREN is generally used as the French business tax identifier. The company must separately request VAT identification from the competent SIE if it makes transactions requiring French VAT identification. A foreign company with a French VAT obligation applies to the SIEE, submitting evidence of incorporation, constitutional documents, business activity, identity and authority of representatives, and details of French taxable transactions. A non-EU-established taxable person generally appoints a French fiscal representative unless an applicable statutory exception or mutual-assistance arrangement applies; an EU-established business generally does not require one. VAT identification does not itself establish a French permanent establishment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SAS is ordinarily subject to French corporation tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS). A qualifying young company may elect temporarily for income-tax treatment under the conditions and time limits in the French Tax Code, including ownership, activity, age, and turnover or balance-sheet tests. Certain qualifying family-owned companies may elect for partnership-style income-tax treatment subject to statutory conditions. France has no US-style check-the-box election; elections do not generally convert the SAS into a fiscally disregarded entity. Hybrid mismatch rules under French law implement applicable EU anti-hybrid provisions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT; taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA), within the EU VAT system. Domestic sales and construction or fit-out services are generally taxable in France when the place-of-supply rules locate the transaction in France; services sufficiently connected with immovable property are generally taxed where the property is located.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a France-established business using the domestic small-business exemption (franchise en base), the general thresholds are EUR 85,000 for supplies of goods and EUR 37,500 for services, subject to statutory higher thresholds, prior-year/current-year tests, exclusions, and amendments. These thresholds are not a general registration safe harbor for foreign businesses: a non-established business making French taxable supplies generally must register from the first taxable transaction unless a specific exemption or reverse-charge rule applies. EU cross-border B2C distance sales are subject to the EUR 10,000 EU-wide threshold where applicable; the EU One Stop Shop may be used for qualifying supplies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing mandatory domestic B2B electronic invoicing and transaction/payment e-reporting. Under the enacted timetable, all businesses must be able to receive e-invoices from 1 September 2026; issuance obligations begin on that date for large and intermediate-sized businesses and on 1 September 2027 for SMEs and micro-enterprises, subject to any later legal amendments. Invoices must pass through an approved private platform (plateforme agréée), directly or through a compatible solution, with required data transmitted to the tax administration. This is not a general real-time pre-clearance or digital-stamping regime. Cross-border transactions and specified transactions outside e-invoicing are generally addressed through e-reporting rules.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods dispatched or transported from France to a destination outside the EU may be exempt with credit (effectively 0% VAT) when statutory export conditions are met and the supplier retains evidence that the goods left the EU. Intra-EU supplies of goods may be exempt only if the customer is VAT-identified in another Member State, the goods are transported there, and reporting and evidentiary requirements are satisfied. Services are not zero-rated merely because the customer is outside France or payment is received from abroad: the general B2B place-of-supply rule, applicable exceptions, and any specific export-related exemption must be assessed. Cleanroom fit-out and services connected with identified immovable property are generally located where that property is situated; French-located work is not converted into an export by a non-French customer. Input VAT recovery remains subject to ordinary deduction rules and valid evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration and export movement reference, including proof of exit from the EU customs territory
Commercial invoice, contract or purchase order, and records identifying the goods and the foreign customer
Transport evidence appropriate to the route, such as bill of lading, airway bill, CMR, or carrier delivery documentation
Evidence of delivery or receipt outside the EU where available
Customer VAT identification and transport evidence for qualifying intra-EU exempt supplies
Bank payment and foreign-exchange records where relevant to transaction substantiation; France imposes no general inward-remittance certificate requirement for VAT zero-rating
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France imposes no general statutory deadline requiring export proceeds to be repatriated to France. Export exemption may be denied and output VAT assessed if the taxpayer cannot establish the export or other exemption conditions; input VAT deductions or refunds may be adjusted, with interest for late payment and applicable tax penalties. Deliberate or fraudulent conduct can attract aggravated penalties and, where statutory elements are met, criminal sanctions. The applicable assessment limitation period is generally three years for VAT, subject to statutory extensions, interruption, or longer periods for specified circumstances.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France); foreign-exchange and financial-sanctions administration delegated to the Direction Générale du Trésor (DG Trésor) of the Ministère de l'Économie, des Finances et de la Souveraineté industrielle et numérique under the Code monétaire et financier.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France maintains full currency convertibility for both current-account and capital-account transactions pursuant to EU Treaty freedom of capital movement (Articles 63-66 TFEU) and the complete post-1989 deregulation of exchange controls. EUR is fully convertible into all deliverable currencies without license, approval, or quota restrictions. Profit remittance from an SAS is freely permitted upon certification of distributable reserves, compliance with legal capital-maintenance rules, and absence of an EU sanctions nexus. Administrative constraints are limited to: (i) balance-of-payments statistical declarations to the Banque de France for cross-border transactions at or above EUR 750,000 per operation; (ii) mandatory sanctions screening; and (iii) enhanced due diligence on flows involving the EU list of non-cooperative tax jurisdictions. No prior government approval applies to dividend distribution, trade settlement, or intercompany funding.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender mechanism or mandatory conversion ratio applies in France. Export receivables may be held indefinitely in EUR or foreign currency, credited to French or EU accounts, or converted at market rate without any timeline constraint. Residual obligations are limited to: (i) statistical reporting to the Banque de France for export transactions exceeding EUR 750,000 per operation; (ii) documentary support for VAT through customs export declarations; and (iii) sanctions and anti-money-laundering screening at the receiving credit institution.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW-to-MEDIUM. ACPR-licensed electronic money institutions (EU-authorised EMIs passporting into France) can provide EUR IBAN accounts, SEPA instant and standard credit transfers, and multi-currency wallet settlement. They cannot, however, issue, confirm, or negotiate documentary letters of credit under UCP 600, provide uncommitted trade finance, or hold capital-escrow funds requiring segregated trust treatment. Non-EU or offshore EMIs are not viable primary banking partners for an SAS due to (i) absence of EU passporting rights, (ii) inability to evidence clearing accounts with the Banque de France, and (iii) rejection of such providers by downstream cleanroom clients and project guarantors. Offshore EMIs should be used only as ancillary disbursement rails for immaterial operational payments, never as the treasury settlement backbone.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French banks normally require the SAS legal representative (Président) to attend at least one physical onboarding interview; directors who are non-EU residents without an existing French banking relationship are typically asked to appear in person or before a notary or certifying officer. Remote account opening with eIDAS-compliant e-signatures is permisible under ACPR digitalised-KYC guidance issued in 2020, but international UBO structures, non-resident ownership, and cleanroom contracting inflows will in practice trigger a physical interview to mitigate fraud and false-invoicing risk. Mandatory onboarding dossier: Kbis extract (issued within 3 months), notarised or certified statutes, UBO registration certificate from the registre des bénéficiaires effectifs, ownership structure chart, board resolution authorising account opening, fiscal situation certificate (avis de situation), EORI and VAT registration proof, and, where applicable, Power of Attorney with certified translation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident or non-EU beneficial owner with an opaque intermediate holding chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) certified organisational chart and UBO register aligned with the registre des bénéficiaires effectifs; (2) apostilled and officially translated certificates of incorporation for all intermediate entities; (3) notarised passport copies of the ultimate beneficial owner(s); (4) OECD/CRS tax residence statements and French Form 5057-equivalent declarations; (5) source-of-wealth report prepared by a regulated adviser; (6) banking references from the country-of-origin bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cleanroom fit-out contracting flows: cross-border procurement plus subcontractor progress payments flagged for false-invoicing risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) two years of audited or reviewed financial statements; (2) signed EPC/main contract and purchase orders referencing cleanroom project scope, stage percentages, and liquidated damages; (3) supplier proforma invoices, delivery dockets, and customs import declarations; (4) Chorus Pro e-invoicing compliance report; (5) subcontractor UBO list with their SIREN/KYB identification; (6) bank statements evidencing historical transaction-pattern consistency.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value capital injection above EUR 50,000 from a foreign parent during initial funding
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) authentic shareholder resolution approving the capital increase and paid-in amounts; (2) share-subscription agreement of the SAS; (3) bank-to-bank provenance letter or recent parent-company account statements proving source of funds; (4) individual source-of-wealth declaration signed by the transferor; (5) payment purpose code and reference narration matching the subscription agreement; (6) receiving French bank's anticipated balance-of-payments declaration and internal KYC memorandum.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments destined to or originating from EU-sanctioned jurisdictions (Russia, Belarus, Iran, Syria, North Korea) or transhipment exposure via third countries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) DG Trésor/SBD export-control opinion where cleanroom HEPA/ULPA filters or HVAC equipment carry dual-use classification under EU Regulation 2021/821; (2) final end-user certificate and end-use undertaking; (3) transactional-level sanctions screening logs; (4) complete supply-chain route with customs transit evidence (ENS/ECS); (5) legal validation by a France-registered commercial attorney; (6) Intrastat and VAT summary returns proving lawful EU circulation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections from non-resident shareholders must be routed via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 to the SAS's EUR account at its French bank, crediting the recipient's full IBAN and BIC. The wire must carry an ISO 20022 purpose code for equity participation (e.g., EQUI), the name and country of the ultimate remitter, and a reference to the share-subscription agreement. The French receiving bank must be pre-advised of the intended inflow to complete (i) sanctions screening of the outside shareholder and any intermediary banks, (ii) the Banque de France balance-of-payments statistical declaration for amounts at or above EUR 750,000, and (iii) internal investment-capital reporting. Upon clearing through TARGET2 (for EUR) or correspondent banking chains, the bank will match the payment to the deposited board resolutions and proof-of-funds dossier; funds may then be segregated into a dedicated Capital Escrow Account and released to the operational account only against documented project commencement milestones and approved drawdown instructions.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: France-based ISIC 4330 cleanroom fit-out contractors may disburse via the following compliant rails: (1) SEPA Credit Transfer (ISO 20022 pain.001/pain.002) for EUR-denominated domestic and EU supplier payments cleared through TARGET2; (2) SWIFT MT103 for USD, GBP, CHF, and other non-EUR payments through correspondent banking; (3) irrevocable Commercial Documentary Letters of Credit (UCP 600) issued via SWIFT MT700 for major cleanroom MEP equipment procurement, payable against checking certificates; (4) Standby Letters of Credit (SWIFT MT760) issued as performance bonds or advance-payment guarantees; (5) documentary collections (DP/DA) for low-risk, established sub-supplier relationships; and (6) milestone-based progress wire transfers matching signed interim payment applications, inspection certificates, and architect/engineer certifications under the construction contract. For outbound trade settlements to the EU and Middle East, back-to-back documentary credits should be used only where sub-suppliers provide matching guarantees or transferable LC terms; otherwise direct telegraphic transfer with conditional release against shipping documents is the preferred treasury posture.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forward contracts (change à terme ferme) in EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF against confirmed trade invoices, with tenors of 1 to 12 months and one-to-one hedging of underlying project exposure

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted Asian currencies (CNY, INR, THB) where cleanroom components are sourced cross-border and executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with an EU/OECD licensed bank, subject to EMIR reporting
Vanilla FX swaps (cambistes) combining spot and forward legs for short-term liquidity bridge financing between project currencies
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP) for long-term intercompany loan hedging, permitted for non-financial counterparties under EMIR when cleared or subject to bilateral risk-mitigation standards
Plain-vanilla FX options (calls/puts) permitted strictly for hedging contingent bid and tender exposures, with premiums expensed under IFRS and no naked trading positions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual RCS non-modification declaration (déclaration annuelle de non-modification)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: RCS / Greffe of the competent Commercial Court via INPI Guichet Unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: One month following the anniversary of RCS registration; annual recurrence (a modification filing during the year satisfies this obligation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal notice from the registry; persistent default may trigger referral to the Public Prosecutor and administrative strike-off (radiation) from the RCS; administrative fine may apply on regularization.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owners (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs) — annual UBO confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: RCS via INPI Guichet Unique (AML/CFT monitoring by Tracfin)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Concurrent with the annual RCS non-modification filing; updates within 30 days following any change in the UBO register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-ordered injunction to regularize; non-compliance may lead to fines up to €7,500 for individuals and €37,500 for legal entities for intentional false declarations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual approval of statutory accounts by shareholders (assemblée générale ordinaire or written consultation), evidencing the procès-verbal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate record book – minutes not filed separately; resolutions may support other RCS filings
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of fiscal year-end (unless court extension granted)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-ordered convocation at company expense; potential judicial supervision for repeated failure; account deposit cannot be completed without an approved shareholder decision.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements deposit (dépôt des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: RCS / Greffe of the competent Commercial Court via INPI Guichet Unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval by the AGO, and in any event no later than seven months after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine up to €1,500 (natural person) or €7,500 (legal entity); persistent non-deposit may lead to an order by the registrar and RCS strike-off procedure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local business contribution (cotisation foncière des entreprises – CFE) declaration and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP (French tax administration) – local corporate tax office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual declaration and payment due by 15 December of the relevant tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 10% of the assessed tax; in case of inaccuracy, additional penalties and interest at 0.20% per month; enforcement action in the event of persistent non-payment.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory external audit (commissaire aux comptes) if the SAS exceeds, for two consecutive years, at least two of the three French thresholds: total balance sheet €4,000,000; net turnover €8,000,000; average workforce 50 employees. Below these thresholds, no statutory auditor is required unless mandated by the bylaws, by one-third of shareholders, or by judicial order.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général – PCG) for individual annual accounts; IFRS as adopted in the EU is permitted only for consolidated accounts of entities so obliged or choosing to do so under applicable accounting rules. Annual accounts must comprise balance sheet, income statement, and notes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SAS must keep an updated UBO register at its registered office and file UBO information with the RCS within 30 days after any change in beneficial ownership. There is no standalone annual UBO tax declaration; however, the annual RCS non-modification filing serves as the annual confirmation that the UBO data remains true and complete. The legal representative should compare the internal UBO register against the latest RCS filing before submitting the annual confirmation; if any change has occurred, the UBO update must be filed before the annual confirmation is accepted.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Registre des mouvements de titres (members' / share transfer register)
Registre des décisions et procès-verbaux (minute book for shareholders' and management/board decisions)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% corporate income tax on taxable profits under Article 219 of the French Tax Code (Code général des impôts, CGI). A reduced 15% rate applies to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit for qualifying small companies, generally subject to annual turnover not exceeding EUR 10 million, fully paid-up share capital, and at least 75% ownership by qualifying individuals or qualifying entities.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: France has no general corporate tax holiday for an ordinary SAS conducting cleanroom construction or interior fit-out. Available incentives may include the 15% SME rate, research and development tax credit at 30% of eligible R&D expenditure in metropolitan France, certain regional investment incentives, innovation-related regimes, and tax depreciation of qualifying assets. The standard participation exemption may substantially reduce taxation of qualifying dividends received by a French parent, generally with a 5% taxable share of expenses and charges, or 1% in certain qualifying French tax group and EU-related situations. French tax consolidation may permit qualifying groups to offset profits and losses. Incentive eligibility depends on statutory conditions, substance, documentation, sectoral limitations, and EU State aid rules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD, corporate income tax return, filed electronically through the impots.gouv.fr professional account using EFI or through an approved EDI-TDFC provider. The return is supported by the applicable tax packages, principally Forms 2058-A-SD, 2058-B-SD, 2058-C-SD, 2059-A-SD to 2059-G-SD, and accounting schedules in the 2050-SD to 2057-SD series. VAT returns and payroll-related declarations are separate. French tax law generally permits indefinite carryforward of tax losses, subject to the annual utilization cap of EUR 1 million plus 50% of the portion of current-year taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million; the schema-prescribed five-year value should therefore not be treated as the operative French statutory rule.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual corporate income tax return. Corporate income tax installments are generally paid four times per year, with a final balance payment. A company with a tax year other than the calendar year files for the relevant accounting period.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a financial year ending on 31 December, the electronic corporate income tax return is generally due by the second business day after 1 May of the following year, subject to the annual administrative calendar. For a financial year closing on a date other than 31 December, the return is generally due within three months after the financial year-end. The balance of corporate income tax is generally payable by the fifteenth day of the fourth month following year-end, with special rules for 31 December year-ends. Quarterly installments are generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December, subject to statutory exceptions and annual calendar adjustments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the SAS legal name, registered office, SIREN number, tax office, fiscal year opening and closing dates, activity description, and whether the company belongs to a tax consolidation group.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder is not entered as the taxpayer merely because it owns the SAS. The French SAS files as a French resident entity. Report the registered French office and French SIREN; disclose foreign parent or group information where requested.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report taxable profit or tax loss, corporate income tax due, tax credits, tax reductions, foreign tax credits where applicable, and the balance payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include the French SAS's worldwide taxable result under French resident-company rules, subject to treaty relief and foreign tax credit rules. Do not exclude income merely because the customer, supplier, shareholder, or lender is non-resident.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identify whether the company is the parent company or a subsidiary of a French tax consolidation group and report relevant group information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign parent does not automatically create a French tax group. French tax consolidation requires satisfaction of specific ownership, election, and eligibility conditions; disclose only legally valid group status.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile accounting profit or loss to taxable profit or loss by reporting permanent add-backs, deductions, exempt income, non-deductible expenses, depreciation adjustments, provisions, finance costs, and tax-specific adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Separate French taxable items from foreign-source items and document treaty or foreign tax credit treatment. Related-party charges must be supported by contracts, benefit evidence, arm's-length pricing, and withholding tax analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report tax losses carried forward, losses used in the current year, current-year losses, and any loss carryback election.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the French utilization cap and maintain schedules by tax year. A change in business activity, merger, or significant restructuring may restrict or eliminate the use of historic losses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the allocation of taxable income or loss within a French tax consolidation group, including group adjustments and subsidiary contributions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete only where the SAS is within a valid French tax consolidation arrangement. A foreign group accounting consolidation is not a substitute for French tax consolidation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report taxable capital gains and losses, including gains on disposals of fixed assets, shares, business assets, and qualifying intellectual property where relevant.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Classify gains under French domestic rules and applicable treaties. Document asset location, ownership period, valuation, and any exemption or participation-exemption analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the allocation and tax treatment of short-term and long-term capital gains and losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not treat a foreign parent's disposal of SAS shares as a French tax item without analyzing French-source rules, substantial participation provisions, real-estate-rich entities, treaty allocation, and anti-abuse rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report qualifying capital gains subject to special rates, deferral, exemption, or sector-specific treatment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use special regimes only where statutory conditions and formal elections are satisfied. Retain legal ownership, valuation, and continuity evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report eligible tax credits and reductions, including the research tax credit and other credits available under current law.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-owned status does not prevent use of a French tax credit, but the expenditure, personnel, R&D, regional, and State aid conditions must be met in France.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report information used for tax calculations and statistical purposes, including value added and employee-related data where required.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use French accounting records and payroll data. Distinguish employees, subcontractors, temporary workers, and personnel supplied by foreign affiliates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report corporate income tax installments, prior payments, credits, and the final balance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile tax payments to the SAS's own tax account. Withholding suffered by a foreign shareholder is not a credit of the SAS unless a specific legal mechanism applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose transactions, payments, or relationships requiring separate forms or schedules, including certain related-party, foreign-account, interest, royalty, and withholding matters.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete additional forms where required for controlled transactions, foreign bank accounts, foreign establishments, withholding, or non-cooperative jurisdictions. A non-resident group company's involvement does not remove French reporting duties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filed corporate income tax returns may trigger a 10% surcharge, increased to 40% in specified circumstances involving formal notice or deliberate non-compliance and potentially 80% for fraudulent maneuvers or abuse of law. Late payment generally attracts late-payment interest of 0.20% per month, subject to statutory rules, in addition to collection measures. Understatement may generate a 40% penalty for deliberate breach, 80% for fraudulent conduct, and 80% in certain abusive arrangements. Failure to provide transfer pricing documentation can trigger a penalty of up to the greater of EUR 10,000 or 0.5% of the transactions covered by the missing documentation, subject to the statutory maximum and applicable reassessment rules.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: The standard French withholding tax on dividends paid by a French company to a non-resident shareholder is generally 25%, subject to treaty relief, EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive implementation, and domestic exemptions. Dividends paid to a qualifying EU or EEA parent company may be exempt where minimum ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax, legal-form, and anti-abuse conditions are satisfied. A 75% rate may apply to certain payments to entities located in non-cooperative states or territories, subject to statutory exceptions and proof requirements.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, the recipient should provide a valid certificate of tax residence and the forms applicable to the income category, generally Form 5000-SD for residence certification and Form 5001-SD for dividends, with the relevant treaty claims completed. The French payer must verify beneficial ownership, treaty eligibility, anti-abuse conditions, holding information, and the recipient's legal status. Where relief cannot be applied at source, the payer withholds at the domestic rate and the recipient seeks a refund through the French tax administration using the applicable forms and supporting documents. Certificates must be renewed or maintained according to French administrative requirements. Treaty relief is not available for conduit arrangements, artificial structures, or benefits obtained in circumstances contrary to the principal-purpose or anti-abuse rules.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties and similar payments from France to non-residents are generally subject to French withholding tax at 25% under Article 182 B of the CGI, subject to treaty reductions, EU interest-and-royalty directive conditions, and special rules for non-cooperative states or territories. Interest paid by a French SAS to a non-resident is generally not subject to French withholding tax under ordinary domestic rules, but exceptions may apply, including certain payments to non-cooperative states or territories, anti-abuse situations, and payments recharacterized as distributions or other taxable income. Treaty rates are country-specific and commonly reduce royalty withholding to approximately 0%-10% and interest withholding to 0%-10%, but the applicable treaty text controls. Form 5002-SD is generally used for interest and Form 5003-SD for royalties when claiming treaty relief or a refund.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400,000,000. Full French transfer pricing documentation obligations generally apply where the French entity or French tax-consolidated group exceeds EUR 400 million of annual pre-tax turnover or gross assets, or where the entity is controlled by or controls an entity exceeding that threshold, subject to the detailed conditions of Articles L.13 AA and L.13 AB of the French Tax Procedures Code. Below the threshold, arm's-length documentation and simplified documentation may still be required where requested by the French tax authority, and the arm's-length principle applies to all controlled transactions. Country-by-country reporting generally applies to groups meeting the EUR 750 million consolidated revenue threshold. Related-party transactions should be identified by category, counterparty, jurisdiction, amount, contractual basis, pricing method, and business rationale.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no standalone UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations regime. French tax authorities apply domestic substance, abuse-of-law, anti-fraud, transfer pricing, beneficial ownership, permanent establishment, and general anti-abuse doctrines. A French SAS must have genuine French functions, decision-making, personnel or appropriately controlled resources, premises or operational capacity where commercially required, accounting records, bank activity, contractual authority, and risk assumption consistent with its claimed business. A cleanroom fit-out contractor should evidence project management, technical supervision, procurement, subcontractor oversight, site activity, health and safety compliance, insurance, customer negotiations, and asset or personnel allocation. Artificial profit booking, circular payments, conduit financing, undocumented management fees, or a company lacking operational capacity may result in denial of deductions, withholding-tax relief, permanent establishment findings, transfer pricing adjustments, penalties, and director or officer exposure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate income tax evasion and fraudulent accounting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing turnover, fabricating subcontractor invoices, recording personal expenditure as project cost, understating progress-billing revenue, maintaining parallel accounts, or deliberately omitting taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, recovery of unpaid tax, late-payment interest, penalties generally ranging from 40% to 80% depending on conduct, and criminal tax-fraud sanctions that may include imprisonment of up to seven years and a fine of up to EUR 3 million, subject to the applicable aggravated-fraud provisions and court findings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors or de facto managers may incur criminal liability, civil liability for personal fault, and tax-payment liability where they have made fraudulent maneuvers or seriously and repeatedly breached tax obligations, including action under the French director tax-liability procedure. Travel restrictions are not automatic; judicial control, passport restrictions, or travel bans may be ordered in criminal proceedings. Imprisonment requires a criminal conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company, artificial substance, or abuse of law
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the SAS solely as an invoicing conduit, booking profit in France without corresponding functions, creating circular transactions, misusing a foreign principal or nominee, or claiming treaty benefits through a conduit entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of deductions, recharacterization of transactions, withholding-tax recovery, permanent establishment or beneficial-ownership findings, 40% or 80% tax penalties where applicable, and possible abuse-of-law penalty of up to 80% of the tax avoided, subject to statutory conditions and committee procedures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for intentional or grossly negligent misconduct causing tax loss, fraudulent management, or criminal participation. Corporate limited liability does not protect a director from personal criminal liability or liability for a distinct personal tort.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's-length management fees, royalties, financing costs, procurement margins, or subcontracting mark-ups to foreign affiliates; shifting cleanroom project profit without functional analysis; or failing to maintain evidence for related-party pricing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary adjustment, possible secondary adjustment or deemed distribution treatment, withholding tax, late-payment interest, and penalties for deliberate or fraudulent understatement. Missing or materially inadequate documentation may trigger the specific transfer pricing documentation penalty and permit assessment based on information available to the tax authority.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil or criminal exposure where pricing manipulation is intentional, fraudulent, or causes insolvency or tax loss. Ordinary pricing disagreement generally creates corporate tax exposure rather than automatic personal liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding tax and profit repatriation failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, royalties, or other taxable amounts to foreign recipients without withholding, applying treaty relief without a valid tax residence certificate, misidentifying beneficial ownership, or failing to remit withheld tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of unpaid withholding tax against the French payer, late-payment interest, applicable 10%, 40%, or 80% penalties, and potential 75% withholding for relevant payments connected with non-cooperative states or territories. The payer may remain liable even where the foreign recipient has already received the payment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director may be personally exposed where failure to withhold or remit results from deliberate misconduct, fraudulent maneuvers, or serious and repeated non-compliance. No automatic personal liability or travel ban arises solely from an ordinary withholding error.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Value added tax fraud and false invoicing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing invoices for work not performed, claiming input VAT on fictitious subcontractor invoices, using incorrect reverse-charge treatment, failing to report construction-related VAT, or suppressing taxable progress payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT reassessment, interest, penalties generally up to 40% for deliberate conduct and 80% for fraudulent conduct or certain abusive arrangements, potential joint and several recovery in fraud cases, and criminal prosecution for aggravated fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for fraudulent invoicing, tax evasion, or knowingly participating in VAT fraud. Courts may impose fines, imprisonment, confiscation, and professional restrictions. Travel bans or passport restrictions require a competent judicial order.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained third-party payments, structuring cash or transfers to avoid controls, processing funds for sanctioned or opaque counterparties, ignoring suspicious payment instructions, or failing to identify beneficial owners and report suspicions where a regulated professional obligation applies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Potential criminal money-laundering sanctions include imprisonment and substantial fines, with aggravated penalties for organized or repeated conduct. Assets and proceeds may be frozen or confiscated. Separate administrative sanctions may apply to regulated professionals and reporting entities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally prosecuted for knowingly laundering proceeds, facilitating prohibited transactions, or obstructing required controls. Confiscation, imprisonment, professional prohibitions, judicial control, and court-ordered travel restrictions may apply; none is automatic merely because a company has an AML deficiency.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Supplying controlled cleanroom equipment, technical components, dual-use items, or services to restricted parties or destinations; falsifying customs classifications, origin, customs value, or end-use documentation; or routing shipments through intermediaries to evade restrictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative or criminal sanctions may include seizure, confiscation, fines, suspension or denial of authorizations, customs recovery, and imprisonment under applicable French, EU, and international sanctions regimes. The exact penalty depends on the instrument, destination, goods, intent, and applicable authorization.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and responsible officers may be prosecuted for knowing or negligent participation where the applicable regime creates such liability. Corporate authorization or delegation does not protect a person who personally ordered, approved, or concealed the conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using undeclared workers, failing to verify foreign subcontractor postings, misclassifying employees as independent contractors, breaching mandatory site safety rules, or using subcontractors without required insurance, declarations, or qualifications.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines, back-payment of social contributions and taxes, exclusion from public contracts, suspension of activity, civil claims, and criminal sanctions including fines and imprisonment for serious undeclared-work or safety violations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The SAS and responsible managers may be liable for labor and safety violations. Directors can face criminal prosecution for personal participation or failure to discharge legally assigned safety duties; civil claims may include employee compensation and restitution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate records, beneficial ownership, and filing non-compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to maintain statutory accounts, filing materially false annual accounts, omitting beneficial-owner information, concealing control arrangements, or submitting false tax or corporate declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines, injunctions, rejection or correction of filings, tax reassessment, director-management bans, and criminal sanctions for false accounts, fraud, or concealment where the statutory elements are satisfied.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur personal criminal liability for false accounts, concealment, or intentional filing misconduct. Insolvency proceedings may impose personal contribution to liabilities or management sanctions where mismanagement caused or aggravated the insufficiency of assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Continuing to incur liabilities while knowingly unable to pay, preferring related creditors, transferring assets below value, destroying accounting records, or repatriating funds before an insolvency filing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Avoidance of transactions, recovery of assets, personal contribution to insufficient assets, management bans, bankruptcy-related criminal sanctions, fines, and imprisonment for fraudulent bankruptcy or related misconduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director may be ordered to contribute to company liabilities, prohibited from managing businesses, or prosecuted where personal misconduct caused or worsened insolvency. Travel restrictions and imprisonment depend on judicial proceedings and conviction; they are not automatic consequences of insolvency.
